- What commit structures (monthly v. annual, phased ramp) and discount ladders do you recommend to avoid overcommit while getting unit discounts?

Can you share a short packaging sketch (numbers rough ok) and any sizing calc you use? Also, would love to schedule a quick call with your solutions engineering team.

Posting quick internal notes before the call:

Summary assumptions (Stratus): median 320 tokens, p95 ~1.1k, peak conc 50–300. Model mixes include both 70B dense and 7–13B quantized variants.

1) Performance posture:
- H100: best perf/$ for 512–1024 token slices when you need low p95. Expect ~15–25% better tail latency vs A100 for same batch once kernels optimized.
- A100: cheaper per-card for memory-heavy single-model footprints (40/80GB), ok for more deterministic batch workloads.
- L40S: strong candidate for quantized weights and lower-cost bulk inference (perf/$ wins for high-volume non-latency-critical routes).

2) Packaging options (commercial):
A) 12-month committed pool (preferred entry)
   - Base commit: $X/month per H100-equivalent slot (we model credits to normalize H100/A100/L40S to H100-equivalents).
   - Discount ladder: 10% at >= 3 months prepay; 18% at 6+ months; 25% at 12+ months annual prepay.
   - Burst credits: 10% of monthly compute as burst pool, additional usage billed at list with retention credit applied.

B) Phased ramp (recommended for cautious adoption)
   - Year 1: 50% commit for 3 months, then ramp to full commit over next 3 months. Discounts pro-rated; guaranteed burst buffer while heating up.

C) Pilot (60-day eval)
   - Lower commit, higher unit price, convertible credit to committed contract within 30 days of pilot end.

3) Sizing guidance:
- For p95 <= 350ms at 512 tokens target: plan for a slab of H100s sized to handle 80% of peak conc (sustained), with an L40S pool for background/quantized requests.
- Use our pool-sizing calc to tune memory tilt: if >30% of requests need >80GB, lean more A100/80GB or H100-80GB variants.

4) Commercial levers to offer:
- Performance-weighted credits (convert unused burst into $ credits for next invoice)
- Graceful downgrade policy for first 90 days (one-time credit if perf shortfall)
- Early-commit discount for 24-month lock (additional 5%)

I'll formalize numbers after the tech deep dive; for the call we should present an H100-primary baseline and 2 mixed-tier variants with per-token perf/$ back-of-envelope.

Hi Priya — answers inline and next steps: 

- Perf/$ table (ballpark):
  • H100: ~ $0.75 per 1k tokens at 512 token average (optimized kernels, low-batch); ~ $1.10 per 1k tokens at 1k tokens due to KV cache pressure.
  • A100 (80GB): ~ $0.85 per 1k tokens at 512 tokens; ~ $1.05 per 1k at 1k tokens — better for memory-heavy single-model cases.
  • L40S: ~ $0.45 per 1k tokens at 512 tokens for quantized paths; ~ $0.70 per 1k tokens at 1k tokens (less efficient on long KV).

  These are rough estimate unit numbers we use to compare packaging; we will run your traces to provide precise per-model per-route numbers.

- Burst credits: monthly allocation (default 10% of committed compute). Unused burst credits do not roll over beyond one billing cycle, but convert to a one-time retention credit if you convert to a committed annual contract within 30 days of the month-end (mechanic used for pilot -> commit).

- SLA: p95 latency guarantee is tied to the pool configuration (the committed slab) and the pinned model version. Our contract includes a named model version and a reference traffic profile; changing model family or payload size outside that profile requires re-baselining. We offer a 90-day grace re-benchmark window during first deployment.

- Pilot conversion: pilot consumption can convert to committed credit up to 100% of pilot usage in the conversion month; above that we true-up at the committed rate. Pilot price differential is refunded as a credit when you sign a qualifying committed contract (within 30 days).

- 24-month early-commit: yes, the additional 5% stacks on top of the applicable ladder (so a 12-month 25% + 24-month early-commit 5% -> 30% total on the baseline). We can model alternate stacking if procurement prefers a flat blended rate.

Next steps: I'll book a 30-min technical deep-dive with Marissa and our infra solutions engineers — propose Tue 2027-05-25 10:00AM PT.
